caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 103 of 1962.
lawyer:
Abdul Quayum, Advocate ----- For the Appellant
Md. Obaidur Rahman Mostafa, AAG ----- For the Respondent
parties:
Khorshed Ahmed Chowdhury ----- Appellant
Vs. 
Government of Bangladesh & others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
2. The suit is for declaration that the khas lands of the plaintiff-Wakf Estate measuring 422.41 acres of khas lands as detailed in schedules A-H have not been legally acquired as excess land as the 70 members of the five families of the name of the wakif Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury, were entitled to retain 700 bighas of khas land under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the order of the Revenue Officer dated 22.2.56 and Circle Officer dated 23.2.56, allowing only 348.80 acres as Khas land of the plaintiff-wake estate, in illegal, null and void. 

 3. The plaintiffs case is the late Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury was a very rich man and he executed and registered the wakfnama dated 14th Ashar, 1337 BS vide Ext.1 with respect to the suit lands. There were tenants with respect to some part of the suit land and the income from the tenanted land would exceed Tk. 10,000.00. Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury had 422.41 acres of khas land in his possession. The wakfnama was duly enrolled with the Wakf Commissioner and its number is 1261. As per the provisions of the Wakf Deed, the wakif Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury was the sole Motwalli till his death. Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury died on 18th Poush, 1341 BS leaving 4 sons namely Fazle Ali Chowdhury, Khorshed Ahmed Chowdhury, Nazir Ahmed Chowdhury and Najibul Hoque Chowdhury. As per the terms of the wakfnama the above 4 sons of Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury were to act as Mutwalli for 2 years only by rotation and in case of death of any son, the son of the deceased would act as Mutwalli. The total income from the wakf estate of Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury from both the tenanted and Khas land was Tk. 30,000.00 per annum. In the Wakfnama, it is stipulated that each son of the wakif Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury would get 60 mds, of paddy and cash of Tk. 2,000.00 annually, The heirs of Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury have got 70 members in 5 families. The Wakf was created for religious, "charitable and pious purposes in conformity with the Wakf Validating Act XI of 1910. It is alleged that no special notification under section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was served for acquiring the Khas land of the Wakf Estate and the above orders are illegal, ultra vires, etc, and the officers of the government have been acting without jurisdiction in acquiring the lands. It is alleged that the number of the members in the 5 families of late Abdul Jabbar is 70, they are entitled to retain bighas of Khas lands in their possession and the Revenue Officer and the Circle Officer have acted illegally and without jurisdiction in acquiring the plaintiff's land in the manner done by the impugned orders dated 22.2.56 and 23.2.56 respectively. The plaintiff was, therefore, obliged to file the present suit for declaration. 

 4. Defendant No. 1, the then Province of East Pakistan, contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, on the grounds that the disputed Wakf is an Wakf-ul Awlad and as such the khas lads of the Wakf Estate has been quite legally and rightly acquired by the impugned orders. The allegations and statements made in the plaint arc not true and the same are denied by the defendant. It is contended in the written statement that the plaintiff and other heirs of late Abdul Jabbar the Wakif have got no right, title and interest in the suit lands which are Wakf properties and they are only the beneficiaries of the wakf. 

 8. It is not disputed that the wakfnana Ext. 1 is a Wakf-al-al-aulad as contemplated under section 20(5)(ii) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such, the wakf property in suit, are liable to be acquired under the above section of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. By the impugned order dated 22.2.56 reproduced in at pages 24-26 Part II of the paper-book, the Revenue Officer allowed 45.36 acres of land to be retained as khas land to meet the expenditure of the charitable deeds mentioned in the wakf deed and 36.39 acres to be retained as Khas land as wakf-al-al-aulad under section 20(5)(ii) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by making the following observation: 

 "Examined the accounts of income and expenditure with the original account which has been audited and checked by the Inspector of Wakf each year. It appears from the accounts attached herewith that the Mutawalli spends Rs. 2,50-1-0 on an average per annum on religious and charitable purposes. On verification it is proved that the Mutawalli actually spends the amounts for religious and charitable purposes. He is, therefore, entitled to be allotted so much of the khas land which will cover the expenditure above and this will be done under section 39(3)(a)(b) of EBSA and T Act of 1950. According to the provision of the section above, the annual net income per acre is calculated at Rs. 56-7-0 as shown in the calculation chart attached herewith. The total expenditure is then determined to Rs. 2,560-7-0 and the net annual profit to Rs. 56-7-0. So 45.36 acres of land is required to meet with the expenditure. The Mutawalli has declared his exercise his option to select land. He may, therefore, be allotted under rule 37 of EBSA Rules, 1951, 45.36 acres of land to retain in his khas possession as Wakf Lillah as shown in Schedule 'B'. This is a mixed big type of Wakf and the Mutawalli 33.06 acres of Khas land and maximum area of 3.31 acres for his homestead which actually covers more i.e 36.37 acres as Wakf-al-al-aulad. As he had declined to exercise his opinion to retain lands he may, therefore, be allotted under Rule 37 the area of 36.39 acres of land to be retained as Wakf-al-al-aulad under section 20(5) (ii) of EBSA and T Act, 1950 vide Schedule 'C'. After allotting all other lands of Wakf Lillah and Wakf-al-al-aulad there are more area of 348.87 acres of lands which may be declared as an excess of the prescribed limit as shown in Schedule 'D' annexed herewith". 

 "In our opinion any wakf-al-al-aulad which is dedicated partly for charitable purpose and partly for individual benefit or wholly for benefit of any individual, the Khas land of such wakf-al-al-aulad estate should be retained on the footing of the living heirs representing the wakf estate on the date the section came into operation. The heirs of the wakif in the aggregate will represent the wakf estate in their representative capacity but not in their personal capacity. Calculated on this basis, the wakf-al-al-aulad estate will retain as much as it will be possible to retain above 100 bighas by as many number as the heirs will be in existence above ten." 

 "According to our judgment, the heirs of the wakf will represent the wakf estate and land will be allotted to the wakf estate on that basis. The land so allotted will be khas land of the wakf estate. If some land in excess is left over on calculation, it will vest in the Government, but the compensation money for the excess land will be wakf and the mutawalli will be bound to re-invest the same in any other suitable property." 

 11. In the present case, the plaintiff claimed that there were 70 members in the 5 families of the heirs of the wak if Mr. Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury and as such they are entitled to retain 700 bighas of Khas land. The learned Subordinate Judge, it appears, did not at all consider this aspect of the case and no issue was framed on the subject. Although the plaintiff's positive case is that they are entitled to retain 700 bighas of Khas land as the individuals in the 5 families of the wakif Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury are 70 in number. 

 12. It may be pointed out that under section 20(2) of the EBSA and T Act a rent receiver may, inter alia, retain in his Khas possession 100 standard bighas of land or 10 bighas for each member of his family whichever is greater. This provision regarding the limit of retainable Khas land was amended and changed. The original ceiling of 100 bighas was raised to 375 bighas by section 4 of Ordinance No. 15 of 1961. But that has again been reduced to 100 bighas by section 5 of PO 98 of 1972. In view of the above position of law and the decision of their Lordships held in the above reported case, it is clear that the Revenue Officer did not comply with the provision of law regarding the area of retainable Khas land by the plaintiff and the learned Subordinate Judge has miserably failed to appreciate the plaintiff's case regarding the area of land, retainable by them on the basis of individual member of the heirs of 5 families of the wakif. 

 13. It is not possible for us to decide here as to the actual number of members in the families of the heirs of late Abdul Jabbar Chowdhury, specially when the learned Subordinate Judge did not at all discuss the point. We therefore, find no other alternative than to send the suit on remand to the Trial Court for framing an issue as to the number of the members of the families of Late Abdul Jabbar and to allow them to retain Khas lands at the rate of 10 standard bighas per member of the families of the heirs of late Abdul Jabbar, as laid down by their Lordships in the above case and also in section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act., discussed above.
